messages: We keep rebuilding ownership directories in docs. Proposal: one developer portal with a canonical service catalog, owners, dependencies, runbooks and production tier.
Harness IDP scorecards are useful, but the goal is behaviour change rather than another dashboard. Start with five checks: owner, runbook, rollback, SLO and dependency freshness.
Decision for ENG-214: continue the Backstage-based pilot and evaluate Harness patterns for scorecards and paved deployment paths before considering a vendor change.
Loop initiative: standardise feature flags and canary cohorts for high-risk releases. Automated health verification must be part of the release path, not a separate checklist.
Do not build another flag wrapper. packages/release-guard already owns cohort assignment, health checks and rollback hooks; extend that contract.
DORA baseline is complete by service tier: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore. These are system signals, never individual developer scores.
Pattern so far: tier-one services with current runbooks recover 38% faster. The next action is improving readiness metadata, not adding more metrics.
Postmortems disappear after review. LOOP-63 links incidents to services, owners, runbooks and repeated failure modes so future designs can retrieve operational lessons.
Code note: incident-linker already extracts service IDs and failure taxonomy from Markdown postmortems. Reuse it before proposing another incident knowledge parser.
